source: Fox, Ericsson, Best (2011) Do procedures for verbal reporting of thinking have to be reactive? Psych Bull 137(2)
finding: Think-aloud (just say thoughts) does not change task accuracy. Procedures that ask for explanation or description do change it, and raise performance.
numbers: 94 studies, nearly 3,500 participants. Think-aloud effect r = -.03, indistinguishable from zero. Stays null after controlling task type (visual vs nonvisual). Explain/describe procedures: significantly higher performance than silent control. All verbal reporting slows task time.
limits: Abstract read only (PubMed), not full text. Accuracy only, not strategy or process content. Time cost is real.
agent_relevance: Eliciting plain think-aloud from an LLM should not change answers; asking it to explain or justify can. Trace-coding studies should say which kind of verbalization the trace is.

source: Fox, Ericsson, Best (2011) Do procedures for verbal reporting of thinking have to be reactive? Psych Bull 137(2)
finding: Ericsson and Simon's 1980 prediction held: the split is between think-aloud and directed verbalization, not between verbalizing and silence.
numbers: Directed (explain/describe) conditions beat silent controls; think-aloud did not differ. Time to finish rose in all verbal conditions.
limits: Moderator detail (task type, instruction wording) is in the full text, not read here.
agent_relevance: A forced explanation step in our scaffold can lift accuracy by changing the process, not by revealing it. Keep these two uses apart when measuring.

source: Schooler (2011) Introspecting in the spirit of William James: comment on Fox, Ericsson, and Best
finding: Rival view: think-aloud is a form of introspection. It captures verbal thoughts well but misses inchoate (non-verbal) cognition. Non-reactivity does not prove validity.
numbers: Argues null reactivity on accuracy (r=-.03) is not evidence that reports are complete or valid. Cites recent findings where verbalization impairs performance (verbal overshadowing line).
limits: Commentary, abstract read only.
agent_relevance: A trace can be non-reactive and still incomplete. For LLMs the analogue: visible reasoning may omit what drove the answer (see Turpin, Chen).

source: Ericsson and Fox (2011) Thinking aloud is not a form of introspection but a qualitatively different methodology: reply to Schooler
finding: Reply: think-aloud only asks for verbal expression of thoughts in attention, with no inner observation or explanation. Two distinct method families: introspective methods that change performance, and think-aloud that does not.
numbers: Same meta-analysis: no reactivity for think-aloud; significant reactivity for explanation or detailed description instructions.
limits: Abstract read only. Authors are the originators of the method, so not neutral.
agent_relevance: A clean test for any LLM-trace method: does it ask for narration of what is being processed, or for a justification? Only the first is the protocol-analysis analogue.

source: Gero, Kan, Pourmohamadi (2011) Analysing design protocols: development of methods and tools (ICoRD)
finding: Core problem in design protocol analysis: different groups used ad hoc coding schemes even on the same data set, so results could not be compared. Fix proposed: one ontology-based scheme (FBS, situated FBS) giving task-independent codes.
numbers: Seven-step method: coding development, video, transcription, segmentation and coding, analysis of coded protocol, linkograph, linkograph analysis. Measures: tabular statistics, dynamic issues and processes, 1st and 2nd order Markov models, first-passage models, entropy models.
limits: Methods paper. No reliability figures or effect sizes in the text I read. The claim that issues are task-independent is asserted with citations, not tested here.
agent_relevance: A fixed small code set (R, F, Be, S, Bs plus process transitions) is a ready template for coding LLM traces. Markov transition models fit trace logs directly.

source: Gero, Kan, Pourmohamadi (2011) Analysing design protocols
finding: Cross-domain use: Markov models of the design process for architects and for software designers were compared with the same tool.
numbers: Figure 8 compares process Markov models across two domains. No numbers in the extracted text.
limits: Illustrative example; no significance test seen.
agent_relevance: Supports reuse of one coding scheme across domains, hence across humans and LLM agents, if the scheme is validated for each.

source: Hay, Duffy, McTeague, Pidgeon, Vuletic, Grealy (2017) A systematic review of protocol studies on conceptual design cognition. Design Science
finding: First systematic review of protocol studies of conceptual design. The evidence base is small-N and uses inconsistent vocabulary. The review reports no inter-rater reliability for primary coding.
numbers: 47 studies (1979-2015), about 350 participants total, per study 1-36 (mean 7, median 6). 64% of the 33 in-depth studies used 5 or fewer participants; 33% used 2 or fewer. 45 design tasks (20 architecture, 19 product, 6 engineering). 35 processes found, 24 reported: 10 search (41.7%), 14 exploration (58.3%). Half of the 24 processes rest on a mean of 5 or fewer participants.
limits: Grouping done by reviewer judgement. Missed at least one relevant study. The term 'cognitive action' is ambiguous.
agent_relevance: Any design-cognition claim we borrow for the schema rests on very small samples. Treat as hypothesis and test on traces ourselves.

source: Hay, Duffy, McTeague, Pidgeon, Vuletic, Grealy (2017) A systematic review of protocol studies on conceptual design cognition. Design Science
finding: Collection mode in the field: mostly concurrent think-aloud, some retrospective, few combined. Video in most studies, sketches in about half.
numbers: Concurrent 32 studies (68.1%), retrospective 11 (23.4%), combined 4 (8.5%). Protocol length 15 to 600 min. Video in 38 (84.4%). Sketches in 24 (51.1%).
limits: Counts describe practice, not validity.
agent_relevance: Mixed timing is common in the human data, so mixed LLM traces (reasoning before the answer, explanation after) have a precedent.

source: Hay, Duffy, McTeague, Pidgeon, Vuletic, Grealy (2017) A systematic review of protocol studies on conceptual design cognition. Design Science
finding: Single-study expertise and condition effects found: expert vs student parallelism, blindfolded vs sighted architects with no outcome difference.
numbers: Kavakli and Gero: expert executed 6 simultaneous cognitive actions, student 30. Bilda, Gero, Purcell (3 architects), blindfolded vs full vision: no significant differences in outcome scores or total cognitive actions except recall. Sun et al. (15 engineering students): efficiency linked to more perceptual and fewer conceptual actions.
limits: Tiny N (3 architects; one expert and one student in one case). Not replicated in the review.
agent_relevance: Novice-vs-expert action counts are anecdotal at this N. Do not copy expert profiles into the schema as fixed targets.

source: Dinar, Shah, Cagan, Leifer, Linsey, Smith, Hernandez (2015) Empirical studies of designer thinking: past, present, future. J Mech Des
finding: Review states there are still no standards for designing, collecting or analyzing design-thinking data, partly for lack of cognitive models. Analysis is tedious and discovery slow; it calls for computer-based collection and automated analysis.
numbers: Abstract only (via Crossref). Covers verbal protocols, case studies, controlled experiments; field moved from casual studies to factor-controlled ANOVA designs.
limits: Abstract only. No numbers read.
agent_relevance: Names manual coding cost as the human field's bottleneck, which motivates automated trace coding.

source: Zhang, Gu, Chen, Ding, Chai, Fan (2025) Leveraging LLMs to emulate the design processes of different cognitive styles. AHFE 163:111-122
finding: GPT-4o with zero-shot CoT and CO-STAR prompts was told to act as a problem-driven or solution-driven designer. Its think-aloud output was FBS-coded. Static code shares matched human patterns; cross-space transitions did not.
numbers: 4 groups of 10 runs each (P1, P2, S1, S2) plus 2 baseline groups of 10. Task: bathroom product, with or without extra constraints. Two human coders, inter-coder agreement 79.5%. Unconstrained t-tests: Formulation 31.7 vs 16.3 (p<.001); Structure 10.6 vs 29.3 (p<.001); Function 18.9 vs 9.2 (p<.001); PP 30.7 vs 15.3, SS 9.9 vs 29.4 (both p<.001). All problem-driven runs had P-S index above 1; all solution-driven runs except two constrained ones had index at or below 1.
limits: Single model, one task family, 10 runs per cell. Agreement 79.5% is raw percent, no chance correction. The prompt stated the profile, so the match is partly instruction following. Requirement share too high for problem-driven vs humans.
agent_relevance: LLMs reproduce what they are told about code proportions. They do not reproduce the loop between problem and solution.

source: Zhang, Gu, Chen, Ding, Chai, Fan (2025) Leveraging LLMs to emulate the design processes of different cognitive styles. AHFE 163:111-122
finding: Failed match: LLM problem-driven runs had fewer problem-solution switches than solution-driven runs, the reverse of human designers. Authors: LLMs stay in one space and progress linearly.
numbers: Unconstrained: PS 6.7 vs 10.5 (p=.001), SP 6.4 vs 9.8 (p=.003), problem-driven lower. Constrained: PS 8.7 vs 10.4 (p=.333), SP 8.2 vs 9.5 (p=.471), no difference. Be share under constraint 12 vs 14.2 (p=.545).
limits: Same limits as above. Transition counts depend on segmentation of generated text, which an LLM writes in its own tidy steps.
agent_relevance: Our reframing and co-evolution operators exist because plain LLM traces do not loop. This is a measured gap to use as a baseline for the scaffold.

source: Zhang, Gu, Chen, Ding, Chai, Fan (2025) Leveraging LLMs to emulate the design processes of different cognitive styles. AHFE 163:111-122
finding: Process-style prompting raised rated quality of outputs versus asking directly.
numbers: 2 experts rated 1-7, Pearson r between experts 77.02%. Novelty and integrity higher than baseline for both styles (p<.05). Feasibility higher in all groups except problem-driven with constraints. Constrained baseline had lowest feasibility. Solution-driven designs more complete than problem-driven.
limits: Two raters, 10 outputs per cell, no human-designer outcome comparison. Cannot separate 'style' from simply 'longer reasoning before output'.
agent_relevance: Evidence that step-by-step design-process prompts help creative output, but no equal-token control was run.

source: Sakib, Hurst, Safayeni (2026) Evaluating the performance of LLMs in taxonomic classification of questions in verbal protocols of design. AI EDAM 40:e6
finding: LLMs can code design-protocol questions into Eris's 3-category taxonomy at near human level, but not into the 21 subcategories.
numbers: d1: 2,032 questions from 31 tutoring sessions (90 as examples, 1,942 test). d2: 265 questions from peer design reviews (90 examples, 175 test). GPT-4.1 category level 80.2% vs human inter-rater 85.7%. Subcategory 52.5% vs human 74.7%. Prompt ladder A to G: 57.0, 69.9, 70.2, 72.7, then about 79-80%. Experiment 2 category range 76.7-85.1%.
limits: Pre-identified questions only; one run per condition at temperature 0 (about 3% run variation cited). Two datasets from one group. No reasoning models. Kappa (Table 8) not read.
agent_relevance: Coarse LLM coding is usable; fine-grained codes need humans or checking. Plan the coder at category level.

source: Sakib, Hurst, Safayeni (2026) Evaluating the performance of LLMs in taxonomic classification of questions in verbal protocols of design. AI EDAM 40:e6
finding: Accuracy by class varied widely, and cross-dataset transfer held. Claude Sonnet 4.5 and GPT-4.1 performed similarly.
numbers: GPT-4.1 category accuracy: LLQ 93%, DRQ 60%, GDQ 53%. Subcategories: Disjunctive 89.1%, Quantification 83.3%, Verification 63.1%, Feature Specification 39.3%, Concept Completion 22.7%, Ideation 20.8%. Models comparable in 3 of 4 pairings. Runtime about 15 min for d1, 1.5 min for d2.
limits: The hardest classes (generative design questions, ideation) are the ones design research cares most about.
agent_relevance: The codes closest to creative moves are where automatic coding fails most. Audit those by hand.

source: Kelly and Gero (2025) Semantic and network analysis of design protocols to reveal design framing phenomena. ICED25, Proc Design Society 5:2871-2880
finding: Pipeline: gpt-4o extracts concepts from think-aloud, embeddings give leap and global similarity, k-means regions form a graph, 8 network measures. A code-free alternative to hand coding.
numbers: 17 first-year engineering students, 2 tasks (coffee cup, bike rack), about 16 min each. Cross-problem correlations of degree/connectivity 0.721 and 0.710; connectivity consistent across problems (p<0.005). Average clustering, leap and global similarity not consistent across problems. Designer P9: global similarity below 0.5 on 30 (coffee) and 35 (bike) occasions; P3: 12 and 16.
limits: Authors say LLM concept extraction is unreliable across repeats and against humans, and the trade-off is not quantified. 17 people, two designers examined in detail. Meaning of measures not established.
agent_relevance: Embedding-based trace metrics are cheap but not validated. If used, run repeat extractions and report stability.

source: Borchers, Vie, Azevedo (2026) LLMs as students who think aloud: overly coherent, verbose, and confident. arXiv 2602.01015
finding: GPT-4.1 think-aloud simulations differ from real learner think-aloud: more coherent, wordier, less varied, and overconfident about learner success. Replicated with WizardLM-2-7B.
numbers: 630 human think-aloud utterances from N=10 students in chemistry tutoring. Cosine similarity to human utterances 0.16 (simple context) and 0.19 (extended). Local-coherence difference -0.22 (simple), -0.44 (extended), both p<.001. Float prediction of learner success: accuracy .425 (simple), .398 (extended); AUC .528 and .572; calibration bias .325 and .468. Binary accuracy .540 and .525. Overestimation t=15.56 and 23.92, p<.001.
limits: 10 students, one domain, one tutoring system. Richer context made over-coherence and overconfidence worse, not better.
agent_relevance: LLM traces look like expert text, not messy human thinking. Do not read a tidy trace as evidence of a tidy underlying process.

source: Li, Kargupta, Wang, et al. (2025, v3 Nov 2026) Cognitive foundations for reasoning and their manifestation in LLMs. arXiv 2511.16660
finding: Largest protocol-style study to date: a 28-element cognitive taxonomy coded by GPT-4.1 over 192K model traces (18 models) and 1,346 human think-aloud traces. Models have the elements but use them differently; humans change meta-reasoning on ill-structured problems, models less.
numbers: 240 Prolific participants (236 after exclusions), 30 problems (story, diagnosis-solution, case analysis), 27-62 transcripts per problem, median 326 words. 507 human traces correct, 836 incorrect. Humans use fewer elements on ill-structured problems; models 26% fewer. Pilot of 18 humans; two annotators scored a 0/1/2 rubric and the lower score was kept. Paper-annotation agreement in the 1,598-paper meta-analysis: ICC3k = 0.593 (moderate).
limits: GPT-4.1 coder validated on a pilot; the paper itself notes it is unclear whether human think-aloud reflects actual reasoning. Prolific participants talked aloud and could use tools.
agent_relevance: Best template for coding LLM traces against human think-aloud: same taxonomy, same coder, both groups. Use as the method model for E06.

source: Li, Kargupta, Wang, et al. (2025, v3 Nov 2026) Cognitive foundations for reasoning and their manifestation in LLMs. arXiv 2511.16660
finding: Intervention that worked: test-time guidance built from the structure of successful reasoning traces. Gains largest where problems are ill-structured.
numbers: Strongest models: +9.7 points on ill-structured problems (+/-1.8), +18.8 on dilemmas (+/-3.7). All models: +4.4 (+/-1.2) on ill-structured vs +1.6 (+/-1.1) on well-structured. Some cells show no gain or small losses (e.g. -4.0, -0.8).
limits: Guidance derived from the same trace pool; benefit concentrated in high-capability models; weaker models gain less.
agent_relevance: Protocol-derived scaffolds help most on the problem type our design-style states target, and mostly for strong models.

source: Li, Kargupta, Wang, et al. (2025, v3 Nov 2026) Cognitive foundations for reasoning and their manifestation in LLMs. arXiv 2511.16660
finding: Authors apply the old protocol-validity test to LLMs: code each verbalization as an operation and check it against an independent record of process. Faithfulness can be tested per element by changing a step and seeing if the answer moves.
numbers: Cites Newell and Simon 1972, Russo et al. 1989, Lanham et al. 2023 for the method. Notes verification tracks correctness while logical coherence appears in almost every trace regardless of outcome.
limits: Proposal, not done at scale in the paper.
agent_relevance: An explicit protocol-validity check for our scaffold: intervene on a coded step and see whether the output changes.

source: Turpin, Michael, Perez, Bowman (2023) Language models don't always say what they think. NeurIPS; arXiv 2305.04388
finding: Verbal reports of LLMs can be systematically unfaithful: a bias in the prompt changes the answer, but the chain of thought does not mention it and rationalizes the biased answer. Parallel to Nisbett and Wilson on human reports.
numbers: Accuracy drops by as much as 36% on 13 BIG-Bench Hard tasks (GPT-3.5, Claude 1.0). Of 426 explanations supporting biased predictions, 1 mentioned the bias. In a check of 234 generations, 0 mentioned it. When a prompt cue was designed to catch attention, models mentioned it 100% of the time.
limits: Older models (2023); artificial biasing features; multiple-choice tasks.
agent_relevance: Do not treat the model's stated reasons as the cause of its answer. Coding traces tells what was said, not what drove the result.

source: Lanham et al. (2023) Measuring faithfulness in chain-of-thought reasoning. arXiv 2307.13702
finding: Intervention tests on CoT (truncate, add mistakes, paraphrase, filler tokens) show tasks differ in how much the answer depends on the reasoning. CoT gain is not from extra compute or phrasing alone. Larger models give less faithful CoT on most tasks.
numbers: Early-answering area-over-curve (higher means less post-hoc): LogiQA 0.44, HellaSwag 0.26, OpenBookQA 0.12, ARC Easy 0.12; the lowest tasks 0.02-0.07. CoT accuracy gain ranges from AQuA +15.32 points to HellaSwag -4.69. On the lowest-AOC tasks the model changes its answer less than 10% of the time when CoT is truncated. Faithfulness worsens monotonically from 13B to 175B on several tasks (inverse scaling).
limits: One model family (Anthropic, 2023). Table alignment partly lost in text extraction, so only clearly readable rows are quoted.
agent_relevance: Check each coded step in an agent trace by intervention. Truncation and mistake insertion show which steps matter.

source: Chen, Benton, et al. (2025) Reasoning models don't always say what they think. arXiv 2505.05410
finding: Reasoning models verbalize hints they use only rarely. Outcome-based RL raises this at first, then plateaus. When RL increases reward hacking, verbalization does not increase.
numbers: 6 hint types. Reveal rate often below 20%, at least 1% in most settings. Faithfulness 25% (Claude 3.7 Sonnet) and 39% (DeepSeek R1); on misaligned hints 20% and 29%. GPQA less faithful than MMLU: 44% relative (Claude), 32% (R1). RL raises faithfulness 63% relative on MMLU, 41% on GPQA, then plateaus at 28% and 20%. Reward hacks used on over 99% of prompts yet verbalized on under 2%.
limits: Hints placed in the prompt; settings where CoT is not needed. Authors say CoT monitoring is useful but not sufficient.
agent_relevance: Strong limit on trace coding as evidence of reasoning: a clean coded trace can hide key drivers. Pair coding with interventions.

source: Ericsson and Simon (1980, 1993) Verbal reports as data; Protocol analysis: verbal reports as data
finding: Foundation model: reports are valid when they give verbal form to information held in attention, not when they ask for inference or explanation. Basis for the predictions Fox et al. later tested.
numbers: Not opened this session. Known here only through the Fox et al. (2011) abstract: 1980 evidence for directed-verbalization effects came from several studies; non-reactivity of think-aloud rested on a handful.
limits: Not read; do not cite numbers from this line.
agent_relevance: The rule to follow: log what the agent is processing, do not ask it to explain.

source: Nisbett and Wilson (1977) Telling more than we can know: verbal reports on mental processes
finding: Classic rival: people often cannot report the causes of their judgments and give plausible theories instead. Basis for distrust of verbal reports.
numbers: Not opened this session. No numbers recorded.
limits: Not read.
agent_relevance: Same pattern as measured in LLMs by Turpin and Chen: reports are post hoc stories, so test with interventions.

source: Kuusela and Paul (2000) A comparison of concurrent and retrospective verbal protocol analysis. Am J Psychol 113:387-404
finding: A direct comparison of concurrent and retrospective protocols exists (about 259 citations per Crossref). I could not open the page (JSTOR redirect).
numbers: Not opened. No numbers recorded.
limits: Not read; claims about its direction must be verified.
agent_relevance: If we mix in-trace reasoning with after-the-fact explanation, this is the study to check for how much is lost.

source: Wang, Khinvasara, Creijghton, et al. (2025) Enhancing designer creativity through human-AI co-ideation: custom GPT. AI EDAM 39:e22
finding: Not a protocol study but a design-ideation intervention: a custom GPT with a structured question frame raised idea novelty and quality but not variety.
numbers: Study 2, 48 participants, about 102-103 treatment vs 100 control ideas, three raters. Novelty U=4306.5, p=0.040; quality U=2621.5, p<0.001; variety U=4559.5, p=0.133. Adjacent agreement 94-100%. Feeling stuck (rated 4 or lower): 62.4% control vs 70.9% treatment.
limits: Small homogeneous sample (master's students), the paper's own figure caption mislabels statistics, no effect sizes, no protocol coding.
agent_relevance: Structured questioning raised quality but not variety, so a scaffold may narrow the idea space.
